entry.label: Metasystem transition
entry.description: A transition in which a new control level forms over lower-level components, producing a new organised whole with additional capacities.
entry.canonical_definition: In the Principia account, emergence of a new level of control over a system or systems.

profile.title: Metasystem transition
profile.summary: The project describes S-prime as containing S-type subsystems and an additional control mechanism. Its scale is the number integrated; the minimum is one, when a new control level appears without replication. Turchin treats integration as necessary but insufficient in his social example.
profile.canonical_definition: In the Principia account, emergence of a new level of control over a system or systems.
profile.why_it_matters: Ask what is controlled, what new controlling mechanism appears, and what evidence demonstrates it.
profile.context_and_lineage: A project-authored account, not evidence of consensus or historical influence.
profile.editorial_note: Paraphrase of attributed authors’ proposals; no endorsement of forecasts or values.
key_distinctions: Aggregation or integration alone does not establish a new control level.
The definition does not establish that an observed transition is beneficial, inevitable, or just.
common_misreadings: Treating a proposed mechanism or normative commitment as a settled conclusion.
open_checks: Source-located research candidates await human editorial acceptance.

connections.scope_conditions: The project describes a metasystem transition as the emergence of a higher level of control. This is Principia's technical specialisation of emergence, not a synonym for every emergent phenomenon.
connections.inference_method: close reading of two project-authored internal theory pages
connections.notes: A metasystem transition is presented as the formation of a higher-level system that controls lower-level systems; the edge now states that specific cross-scale claim.
connections.plain_phrase: specialises emergence as a new higher level of control within
